newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kobe Steel passes screening to sell electricity.
newsitem.headline: Kobe Steel passes screening to sell electricity.

text.p: Kobe Steel Ltd said on Tuesday it had passed an initial screening to sell electricity it plans to generate at its plants to Kansai Electric Power Co.
The companies said they hope to work out the final details and sign a contract by mid-December.
Kobe Steel hopes to supply 54,500 kilowatts of electricity generated at its Kakogawa plant in western Japan to the power company starting from April 1999, the steel maker said in a statement.
Kobe Steel also hopes to start supplying 659,000 kilowatts from its Kobe plant in April 2002, the statement said.
Kansai Electric also said three other companies, Nippon Steel Corp, Osaka Gas Co Ltd and Nakayama Kyodo Hatsuden KK, an affiliate of Nakayama Steel Works Ltd, passed the initial screening phase.
